newsitem.title: ITALY: De Benedetti quizzed in Italy insider trade probe.
newsitem.headline: De Benedetti quizzed in Italy insider trade probe.

text.p: Carlo De Benedetti, former chairman of Olivetti, was questioned for four hours on Wednesday by Italian magistrates investigating allegations of insider dealing in the information technology group's shares.

De Benedetti, who is now honorary chairman after resigning his executive post in September, told reporters as he left the magistrates' offices here: "We have demonstrated with documents the total lack of substance behind the insider trading theory."

Turin magistrates have been investigating allegations of insider trading in Olivetti shares during a period in August shortly before the company published half-year accounts which revealed further losses at the struggling group.
De Benedetti was accompanied by his lawyers when he left the offices of magistrates in northeastern Turin at around 1330 GMT on Tuesday.

A statement from lawyers Gilberto Lozzi and Cesare Giordanengo said: "Engineer De Benedetti presented himself before magistrates today and clarified in the course of questioning all aspects of the matter, showing with documents that the hypothesis of insider trading is totally groundless."
The Turin investigation is not the only probe into the flamboyant financier's loss-making group in recent months.

Stock market regulator Consob is also carrying out its own inquiry into Olivetti's first half 1996 accounts after a senior manager resigned in September saying he did not agree with all the figures in the six-month report.
Magistrates in Olivetti's home town of Ivrea, close to Turin, also opened a preliminary inquiry into the company's accounts in September.
